method.parsing: node/grep over saved HTML + CSS; no JS execution, no headless browser
method.caveat: All values below are static: declared CSS, not computed style. Where a value depends on cascade order or JS-applied classes it is marked inferred or set to null.

pagesNote: Both pages are server-rendered: real heading and body text is present in the initial HTML (no bot challenge, no empty shell). The very low text-to-HTML ratio is not a JS shell — it comes from ~320KB of inline atomic <style> and a large serialized React state payload per page. /api/charges alone ships 1.75MB of HTML for 15KB of prose (0.84% text).

stylesheets.role: docs-specific component CSS (article, sidebar, code blocks, print)

stylesheetsNote: Only 2 external stylesheets, both from b.stripecdn.com; their <link> hrefs are UNQUOTED in the markup. No @import anywhere. 11 inline <style> blocks (2 pairs byte-identical across the two pages). Deduplicated total analysed: 529,240 bytes of CSS. All selectors are prefixed with a repeated zero-width-space id selector (#\u200b x7-10, matching <html id="\u200b">) purely as a specificity multiplier — a measured fact, stripped before analysis.

typography.system: Sail design system. Two layers: named tokens (--sail-font-*, --sail-font-size-N) in the base sheet, and hash-named atomic tokens (--s-1joebgy, --as-5g …) generated by a CSS-in-JS compiler in the inline blocks. All values below are resolved through the var() chains.

fontStacks.stack: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif, 'Apple Color Emoji', 'Segoe UI Emoji', 'Segoe UI Symbol'

typography.fontStacksNote: No webfont. Zero @font-face rules and no fonts.googleapis.com link — the whole docs site runs on the system UI stack, with per-language CJK stacks swapped in via html:lang(). Monospace is the only place a named family ('Source Code Pro') appears, and it still falls back to system mono.

fontSizes.note: declared token --sail-font-size-28, unused on these pages
declared token, unused on these pages
declared token, unused on these pages

typography.fontSizesNote: Overwhelmingly absolute px (rem appears 4 times in the whole 529KB corpus, em only for badge-relative sizing). Nothing scales with the root font size.
typography.lineHeightsNote: Line height is declared in absolute px, not as a unitless ratio, in ~95% of cases. This is a hard vertical rhythm: every text style is a fixed (size, leading) pair, and the pairs land on 4px multiples (20/24/26/32/40).

h2.reason: In-article h2 (class "Heading Heading--anchored") carries NO font-size in any screen rule — docs.css sets only `article h1,h2,h3,h4,h5{font-weight:700}` and `article h2{padding-top:32px}`. Its size therefore comes from the UA default (1.5em) against an inherited size that cannot be resolved without computed style. Not guessed.

ratio.note: Not a geometric scale. Resolvable steps are 32 -> 24 -> 16 -> 16 (1.33x then 1.5x then 1.0x): h3 and h4 are the same size and separated only by weight (700 vs 600) and spacing. Body is 16px, so h3 == body size. Differentiation is by weight and space, not size.

headingScale.printOverrideNote: docs.css also defines .Article--ApiReference h1/h2/h3 at 15px/13px/11.5px — these live inside @media print and were excluded from the screen scale.

bodyCandidates.note: Two distinct body sizes by region: 16px/26px for prose inside <article>, 14px/20px for every piece of application chrome (sidebar, header, tables, API-reference parameter rows). This is the concrete mechanism behind 'technical reference made app-like' — prose gets reading measure, the surrounding UI gets a denser app scale.

typography.fluidTypeEvidence: clamp() appears 8 times in 529KB, all inside Sail's cap-height baseline-alignment math (--s--transform-align-y, margin-top/bottom corrections) — zero occurrences of clamp() or vw in any font-size declaration. vw is used only for widths and one row-gap:2.5vw. Type is fixed px at every breakpoint.

spacing.evidence: The design system declares its own scale explicitly as --sail-spacing-0/2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/48/64/80 — every step above 2 is a 4px multiple. Resolving all margin/padding/gap declarations through their var() chains confirms it: the nine highest-frequency values are 6, 16, 12, 8, 4, 20, 24, 32, 40. 4px multiples cover 67.3% of weighted spacing usage; 2px covers 85.8%.
spacing.exceptions: 6px is the single highest-frequency value (495) and is NOT on the declared token scale, so it comes from component-local CSS rather than tokens. 1px/2px/3px/5px are largely borders, focus rings and optical nudges, not layout rhythm.

color.system: Sail palette: 11 hues (gray, blue, cyan, green, yellow, orange, red, purple, violet, and neutrals) x 10 steps (50-900), each declared as an -rgb triple token plus an rgb() wrapper token. 235 --sail-color-* tokens, 224 of them colour-valued.
color.twoPalettes: Two full palettes ship in the same sheet: a default set on :root and a 2021 refresh on html.sail-color-2021. Neither page's <html> carries that class (markup is <html id="\u200b" lang="en-US">), so the :root values are the live ones. Both are recorded below where they differ.
color.customPropertiesNote: Capped at 50 named, colour-like tokens out of 224. Excluded: 1,692 total custom properties in the corpus, the great majority hash-named atomic tokens (--s-1joebgy etc.) generated by the CSS-in-JS compiler and meaningless as a vocabulary.

backgroundCandidate.note: Page ground is a cool off-white, not pure white; article surfaces sit on white (--sail-color-background / .SampleApp{background-color:#fff}).

contrastRatioCandidate.wcag: passes AA and AAA for normal text in both cases
contrastRatioCandidate.provenance: measured (computed from the two resolved values)

color.darkModeEvidence: Only 2 @media(prefers-color-scheme: dark) blocks in 529KB, both scoped to component opt-ins: one sets color-scheme:dark on .as-0, the other retints a `.sn-token-provider` widget's tokens (#03143d, #051a4c…). No [data-theme]/[data-color-mode]/[data-appearance] selector exists anywhere; <html> carries no theme class or attribute; no theme toggle control is present in the markup. The docs are light-only, with dark handled as a per-component exception.

layout.breakpointsNote: 111 media queries, 32 distinct width thresholds — no tidy 4-or-5-step ladder. One real breakpoint dominates: 1000px (30 of 111 queries, min and max) is where the sticky right-hand code pane appears and the layout goes from one column to two. Everything else is component-local. Mostly max-width, i.e. desktop-first authoring.

layout.contentColumnFormula: width: calc(100vw - var(--sidebar-width) - var(--assistant-width) - var(--xray-open) * var(--xray-width)) — the article column is computed by subtracting each optional panel from the viewport, so opening the AI assistant or the 'xray' panel narrows the prose rather than overlaying it.

gridUsage.note: Flexbox is the layout engine (94 display:flex vs 9 display:grid). Grid appears only for card galleries: repeat(2,1fr), repeat(3,minmax(200px,33%)), repeat(auto-fill,minmax(300px,1fr)), repeat(12,1fr).

measurement.notes: Static-only extraction: curl + node/grep, no JS executed and no computed style read. Both pages returned HTTP 200 with server-rendered prose, so nothing is blocked or JS-shelled. Limits of this method, stated honestly: (1) Stripe compiles its styles to hash-named atomic classes and hash-named custom properties, so every reported value was obtained by resolving var() chains through the deduplicated 529KB corpus — chains were followed to a maximum depth of 8, and where a token has two definitions in different scopes both are reported rather than one being chosen. (2) In-article h2 size is genuinely unresolvable statically and is null. (3) Which --sidebar-width (250 vs 280) and which palette (:root vs .sail-color-2021) is live depends on JS-applied classes; the :root palette is reported as live because <html> carries no class in the delivered markup. (4) @media print rules were stripped before deriving the screen heading scale. (5) Byte counts are decompressed on-disk sizes; compressed wire sizes are recorded separately. (6) Occurrence counts are declaration counts in CSS source, not counts of elements actually painted.

browserPass.tool: Claude Code Browser pane (Chromium), computed styles via javascript_tool
browserPass.notes: Desktop emulated at 1440x900; the pane's own desktop preset reported a 0x0 viewport.

measured.method: Chromium computed styles read via javascript_tool. Desktop emulated at 1440x900 because the pane's own 'desktop' preset reported innerWidth/innerHeight of 0; mobile at the 375x812 preset with a reload. Characters per line = paragraph content-box width divided by the average glyph width of a 100-character lorem span rendered in the paragraph's exact computed font styles.

readingColumn.fontFamily: -apple-system, system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
readingColumn.backgroundFrom: main (first ancestor with a non-transparent background)
readingColumn.note: The prose column is 503px inside a 1160px <main>; the remaining width is the paired code/response panel. The reference page is dark by default at this viewport, not a user preference: colorScheme computes to 'normal' and no prefers-color-scheme emulation was set.

headings.h2Reason: No rendered non-empty h2 exists on the Charges API reference page; the page goes h1 (page title) to h3 (endpoint and attribute headings).

chrome.scrollOwnerNote: documentElement.scrollHeight stays at the 900px viewport height; the article scrolls inside <main>, and the left navigation scrolls inside its own 280px pane (clientHeight 762, scrollHeight 4760).
chrome.stickyPattern: Nine sticky (never fixed) 503px-wide 'ApiSection-Aside' panels at top:16px, one per endpoint section: the code sample tracks its prose section and releases at the section boundary.

desktop.tocReason: No element matching an on-this-page pattern with three or more in-page anchors, sized 80-460px wide, was found. Section navigation is carried by the persistent 280px left endpoint list instead.

search.triggerBehaviourReason: A single <kbd>/</kbd> hint is in the DOM, but no search input or labelled search control renders at load, and the key was not pressed, so what it opens is not determined. The 'Search charges' links found by an aria/text scan are API endpoint links, not site search.

mobile.typeScaleNote: Body 14px/22.4px and h1 24px/32px are identical at 1440px and 375px. The layout adapts by column count, not by type size.

chrome.note: At 375px the page renders no <header>, no <nav>, no sidebar scroll pane and no element whose class or aria-label matches menu/nav/hamburger/toggle. The desktop 56px header and 280px endpoint list are removed from the DOM rather than collapsed behind a control.

mobile.codeAsideNote: The 'ApiSection-Aside' code panels stay position:sticky at top:16px but are now 319px wide — the same width as the prose — so the two-column prose/code pairing has stacked into one column.

inferred.intersectionObserverNote: Not found in the 17 script sources or the inline script text scanned; the sticky code panels are pure CSS position:sticky, which needs no observer.
inferred.hoverPreviewMarkerNote: Count of elements matching [data-tooltip] or a class containing tooltip/hovercard/popover/preview. Presence only; no hover was performed, so the behaviour is not confirmed.
inferred.readOfInterest: 1377 custom properties resolve on :root — the design tokens are shipped as CSS variables, and the class names are hashed two-character atoms (as-9, rs-2), i.e. an atomic CSS build, not authored class names.
